issues.issue: The provision opens mid-sentence ("time of acceptance of this agreement by the Court"), so the operative obligation it attaches to is missing, and "fails to comply" is not tied to any standard of materiality or to a deadline. A court would have to reconstruct what condition is being imposed and what degree of non-performance triggers redocketing.

The sentence is garbled and incomplete ("On the charge(s) Jn this. 'Casey etees that it thé vent that the Defend, fails to comply"), so it is unclear whether the jury waiver is unconditional or operates only if prosecution is resumed. The mechanical defect changes the reach of a constitutional waiver.

The admission breaks off mid-sentence ("the Defendant admits that he and the victim got into an argument and"), leaving the scope of what is actually admitted unresolved. A court asked to treat the stipulation as a binding admission would have to construe how far the incomplete "Specifically" sentence qualifies the preceding general stipulation.

The stipulation of guilt-establishing facts sits against paragraph V.E (c012), which promises that information given by the Defendant "will not be used against Defendant if this cause is redocketed and prosecution is resumed," and against V.C's promise that compliance information stays non-public. Whether the stipulation is inside or outside that use-protection is a genuine internal inconsistency.

The clause requires payment "as instructed at the time of signing this agreement" but then states "Payment in full due by March 11, 2011," giving two different payment dates in one sentence. A court would have to decide which controls for compliance purposes.

"Not commit any criminal offense" does not say whether an arrest, a charge, or a conviction establishes a breach, and it covers any offense however trivial. The garbled reference to the "ten [term] of this agreement" leaves the covered period undefined on the face of the clause.

"Any evaluation and counseling information would be reviewable by the Prosecutor ... but would not otherwise be available to the public or for publication" names no obligor and no enforcement mechanism, and "available to the public" is undefined. A court would have to construe whether this creates an enforceable confidentiality duty on the State.

"This information will not be used against Defendant" does not say whether it covers only answers to inquiries or everything the Defendant supplied under the agreement, and "all reasonable inquires" posed by "all Law Enforcement Agencies" has no stated boundary. Both the subject and the scope of the use-immunity are open to competing readings.

The use-immunity here cannot be squared with paragraph IV.C (c007), in which the Defendant stipulates to the facts of the battery for use if prosecution resumes. Read together, one clause supplies the State with an admission and the other withdraws it.

"The date by which the Defendant is to be dismissed from the Pretrial Diversion Program" is ambiguous between the date the charges are dismissed, the date the diversion term ends, and a deadline for the State to act. The word "dismissed" carries opposite connotations (successful exit versus expulsion) in this context.

The acknowledgment says non-compliance means the agreement "will automatically be revoked," while paragraph II (c002) makes it the Defendant's responsibility to show completion and provides only that the case "will be redocketed" and prosecution resumed. Whether revocation is automatic or requires prosecutorial or judicial action is left unreconciled.
